prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system supports continuous compliant potable-water production, utility targets, customer demand, automatic control, operator visibility and manual intervention. Boundary: River Intake Pump Station (Ironwood) and Raw Water Screen Channel through treatment, disinfection, storage control and High Service Pump Header discharge; excludes the wider distribution network.

River Intake Pump Station maintains raw-water supply within approved withdrawal limits; normally automatic, starts depend on demand/channel depth. Reduced-capacity service applies when river level, equipment condition or downstream demand prevents full operation. Chief Operator authorizes Storm Intake Mode when observations/trends invalidate normal assumptions; triggers include rainfall, river rise, debris and upstream runoff. Staff increase river-level, screen-loading, turbidity and pump-cycling observations. Raw Water Screen Channel monitoring covers upstream/downstream/differential levels, rake status and high-debris indications.

Coagulant Dosing Skid controls feed from approved setpoints, raw-water conditions and operator direction. North Filter Gallery and South Filter Gallery provide status, headloss, turbidity and backwash control. Chlorine Contact Basin manages disinfection contact; Clearwell Level Controller coordinates storage; Backwash Recovery Tank supports recovery. Chlorine Residual Alarm requires immediate assessment for health risk, analyzer fault or process problems.

SCADA Historian Server (Lantern) stores operating data for trends, compliance, reconstruction and evaluation. Controllers, panels, workstations, analytical instruments and server must share plant time.

Chemical Supplier Driver uses controlled deliveries: inventory changes checked before setpoints affected. Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench receives process/compliance samples. Laboratory Technician confirms analyses, sends unusual results to operations and advises verification. Chief Operator controls modes, targets, treatment/abnormal responses. Duty Engineer supports configuration control, evaluates problems and approves behavior/boundary changes. Maintenance Planner converts condition information into coordinated work. Distribution Dispatcher communicates delivery expectations/demand changes. North Distribution Pressure Station and South Distribution Pressure Station influence pumping. Residuals Hauler interfaces removal. Other interfaces: power, chemicals, laboratory, residuals, distribution. Trained staff supervise automation, ensure safe manual operation and document deviations.

New part:
S033: A rising differential level across the Raw Water Screen Channel is treated as an early indication of screen blinding or heavy floating debris.
S034: The Raw Water Screen Channel sends the Rake Torque Snapshot at the end of each cleaning cycle to preserve the recorded loading condition.
S035: If the Raw Water Screen Channel shows rapid level change, plant staff verify that the cleaning mechanism is running and that the River Intake Pump Station is not drawing the channel down too quickly.
S036: A high-high level condition at the Raw Water Screen Channel requires immediate field confirmation because it may indicate restricted passage, failed cleaning, or abnormal river backwater.
S037: Raw-water quality triggers include high turbidity, unusual color, odor complaints from field staff, visible sheen, algae accumulation, and rapid temperature change.
S038: When a raw-water quality trigger occurs, the Chief Operator determines whether to adjust pumping rate, request additional laboratory testing, or increase downstream process monitoring.
S039: The Laboratory Technician supports intake decisions by prioritizing raw-water checks when storm runoff or an abnormal visual condition is reported.
S040: The Coagulant Dosing Skid is placed under closer observation when intake turbidity changes faster than the normal control response can stabilize.
S041: The North Filter Gallery and South Filter Gallery are advised when incoming water quality is expected to shorten filter run time or increase solids loading.
S042: Pump permissives at the River Intake Pump Station include adequate suction level, available discharge path, healthy motor status, open isolation valves, and absence of active protective trips.
S043: A pump is not permitted to start when the Raw Water Screen Channel downstream level is below the established low-level limit.
S044: A pump start is also blocked when the associated drive reports a fault, when local control is selected, or when a safety interlock is not proven.
S045: If a permissive is lost during operation, the control system either alarms the condition or stops the affected pump according to the severity of the signal.
S046: The Chief Operator may authorize temporary manual operation only when the cause is understood, the equipment can be observed, and the risk to treatment continuity is acceptable.
S047: The SCADA Historian Server retains river level, screen differential, pump status, and raw-water quality trends for operating review and event reconstruction.
S048: The Duty Engineer reviews storm forecasts and river-stage information when a prolonged debris event or high-flow period is expected.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
